system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
prompt:

Hey Spotify, why is it that when I buy a $10 prepaid card to purchase the 3 month re-enrolling offer, I have to enter my card information as well? The offer is for $9.99 so it should work, but it feels like you're double dipping just to have my card information.

     spotify replied: Hey there. That's not cool. Can you try using an incognito window or private browsing session to get the deal? Let us know how it goes

[2545863] past customer: so why cant we come in contact with spotify? And why cant I change my credit card for my subscription? All I get is a stone dead "change payment details" site...
     spotify replied: Hey there! You can get in touch with our email/chat support teams at <link> but we can also help you here. Are you getting any specific errors when trying to update your payment details?

[926722] past customer: my spotify premium ended i need to buy another card for 3 months asap
     spotify replied: Hey there! You can buy gift cards here: <link> We'll be right here if you have any questions 🙂

[2251784] past customer: I️ need to contact someone about cancelling a membership that was used with my card. I️ have never used Spotify! #GetAContactNumber
     spotify replied: 2: your statement? It usually starts with "P03". We'll take a look backstage /GT <link>

[2162586] past customer: hello! does spotify still take a visa gift card as a form of payment for premium?
     spotify replied: Hey there! We accept gift cards as long as these requirements are met: <link> Hope this clears things up

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
Hey there. That's not cool. Can you try using an incognito window or private browsing session to get the deal? Let us know how it goes

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hey there! Can you DM us your account's username and email address? We'll take a look backstage /SY <link>

Return the JSON scores.
